questions.question: Describe four ways in which people in West Africa were enslaved and explain what happened on the march to the coast.
questions.expected_answer: Captured in war; seized in raids or kidnapped (like Equiano); sold as punishment for crimes or accusations; sold for debt or during famine. They were tied together in coffles and marched for weeks or months to the coast, often sold several times; many died of hunger, thirst, exhaustion, disease or violence.

questions.question: Using evidence such as the Brookes plan and Equiano's account, describe conditions on the Middle Passage and two forms of resistance.
questions.expected_answer: The voyage took about 6-10 weeks; captives were chained in pairs below deck in cramped, dark, hot, filthy spaces (the Brookes plan shows people packed like cargo); disease spread, food and water were poor, crews were brutal and women were abused; about 1 in 7 or 8 died. Equiano described the stench, cries and his wish to die. Resistance: refusing food, jumping overboard, revolts on about one in ten voyages.

questions.question: Describe how enslaved people were sold in the Americas and where most were taken.
questions.expected_answer: They were washed and prepared, then sold at public auctions to the highest bidder, in scrambles where buyers rushed to seize captives at fixed prices, or privately; families and shipmates were separated. About 45% went to the Caribbean, about 40% to Brazil, about 5% to Spanish America and about 4% (around 400 000) directly to mainland North America, where an internal trade later moved about a million people to the Deep South.
